title: 夜书所见
titleEn: Written at Night About What I Saw
author: 叶绍翁
intro: Autumn wind in the parasol trees makes a traveller think of home — and then he sees a lamp in the dark where children are hunting crickets, just as he once did. A tender poem about memory and distance.
analysis: 这首诗写一个在外地的人，秋夜里想家。第一句写声音：秋风吹过梧桐树，叶子萧萧作响，好像把寒意一阵阵送过来。第二句点明心情：江上的秋风，勾起了游子（离家在外的人）的思乡之情。后两句画面一转：远处篱笆边，夜深了还亮着一盏灯，作者猜想，一定是孩子们在那里捉蟋蟀吧。“挑促织”就是用草拨弄、逗引蟋蟀。为什么写孩子？因为这让作者想起自己小时候在家乡也这样玩。孩子们的快乐和作者的孤单形成对比，那盏小小的灯，既是孩子们的灯，也照亮了作者对童年和家乡的回忆。前两句写冷清，后两句写温暖，冷暖对照，思乡的情绪写得含蓄又真切。
analysisEn: A man far from home spends an autumn night thinking of it. The first line is all sound: the wind rustles through the parasol trees, and the leaves seem to send the cold toward him in waves. The second line names the feeling: the autumn wind over the river stirs a traveller’s longing for home. Then the picture changes. Far off, by a bamboo fence, one lamp is still burning late at night, and he guesses that children must be out there hunting crickets. 挑促织 means teasing a cricket out with a blade of grass, a favourite game of Chinese children for centuries. Why write about children? Because they remind him of himself as a boy, playing the same game at home. Their fun and his loneliness sit side by side, and that small lamp lights both their game and his memories. The first half is cold and lonely, the second half warm; the contrast lets his homesickness show without his ever saying “I miss home”.
background: Ye Shaoweng (dates uncertain, active early 13th century) was a Southern Song poet who spent much of his life in retirement near West Lake in Hangzhou. He is best known for short, fresh quatrains like this one and “Visiting a Garden but Not Finding Anyone In”.
pronunciation: 挑促织 tiǎo cù zhī：“挑”读第三声 tiǎo（拨弄、逗引），不读 tiāo。萧萧 xiāo xiāo；篱落 lí luò。
version: 采用通行教材文本。“挑促织”在《江湖小集》（四库本）中作“捉促织”，网站用教材的“挑”。

lines.py: xiāo xiāo wú yè sòng hán shēng
lines.lit: Rustling parasol leaves send a cold sound;
lines.en: Parasol leaves rustle, sending sounds of cold;

lines.py: jiāng shàng qiū fēng dòng kè qíng
lines.lit: autumn wind on the river stirs a traveller’s feelings.
lines.en: the autumn wind on the river stirs a traveller’s heart.

lines.py: zhī yǒu ér tóng tiǎo cù zhī
lines.lit: I know there are children teasing crickets;
lines.en: Children must be out there, coaxing crickets —

lines.py: yè shēn lí luò yī dēng míng
lines.lit: late at night by the fence, one lamp is bright.
lines.en: deep in the night, one lamp glows by the fence.

words.note: 象声词，现代汉语书面语也用。

words.en: the sound of cold; chilly sounds
words.note: 指秋风吹叶的声音，带着寒意。
“客”是离家在外的人；现代汉语“客人”意思不同。
读第三声，用细长的东西拨弄；现代汉语“挑逗”。
古代叫法；现代汉语说“蟋蟀”，北方叫“蛐蛐儿”。

imagery.name: 梧桐
imagery.zh: 秋风里萧萧作响的梧桐叶，带来秋天的寒意和游子的愁绪。
imagery.en: The rustling parasol leaves bring the chill of autumn and a traveller’s sadness.

imagery.name: 秋风
imagery.zh: 江上的秋风直接勾起了作者的思乡之情。
imagery.en: The autumn wind on the river is what stirs his homesickness.

imagery.name: 灯
imagery.zh: 篱边一盏灯是孩子们捉蟋蟀的灯，也点亮了作者对童年和家乡的回忆。
imagery.en: The lamp by the fence lights the children’s game — and his own memories of childhood and home.
